drug_class: Integrin receptor antagonist (a type of biologic medication)
purpose: Vedolizumab is used to treat adults with moderate to severe Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps reduce the inflammation in your gut that causes symptoms like stomach pain, diarrhea, and bleeding. The goal is to help you feel better and keep your condition under control for the long term.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly sends too many inflammatory cells into the lining of your intestines, causing damage and symptoms. Vedolizumab works by blocking a protein that acts like a 'gate' that lets those harmful immune cells enter your gut. By blocking this gate, the medication reduces inflammation specifically in your intestines without broadly suppressing your entire immune system.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, joint pain, nausea, fever, upper respiratory infections like a cold, tiredness, cough, and bronchitis. Most people tolerate this medication well. Some people may have a mild infusion reaction during or shortly after their IV treatment, such as feeling flushed, having chills, or a mild rash.
warnings: Let your doctor know if you have any infections before starting this medication, as vedolizumab can lower your ability to fight certain infections. Tell your healthcare team right away if you develop signs of a serious infection such as high fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms that are severe. It is important to get all recommended vaccinations before starting treatment. Also let your doctor know if you have liver problems or a history of tuberculosis. This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, so discuss this with your doctor.
typical_dosing: Vedolizumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion at a clinic or infusion center, usually over about 30 minutes. The typical schedule starts with doses at Week 0, Week 2, and Week 6, and then every 8 weeks after that for maintenance. There is also a subcutaneous (under-the-skin) injection form available for maintenance dosing every 2 weeks after the initial IV doses. Your doctor will decide the best dosing schedule for you.
